turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale. I have until 4:40. Why was Owen's zero in the gradebook before anyone called me?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
"The end of it." Turnitin's own guide says that number shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student, and your procedure 4.3 says the same. So what else do you have, Hale?
I don't need more proof than that.
"I don't need more proof." I'm writing that down, word for word. Your own procedure says otherwise, and I'm happy to take it upstairs to the principal if that's your answer.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
"Unlike some people." Who, exactly? My son never lies, and if you're saying that about me, say it plainly so I can write it down properly.
"Zero stands." Okay. Then I'll have your name, your reasons and procedure 4.2 in an email to the principal tonight, and you can explain to her why you entered a mark before calling me.
